objects: small and large regression signals; Gaussian and double exponential priors
assumptions: high-dimensional shrinkage with small and large signals
conclusion: Single-scale Gaussian and double exponential priors are insufficiently flexible, and concentrating the double exponential near zero to shrink small signals over-shrinks larger signals.
scope: Author motivation for flexible shrinkage priors.
span: For example, in high-dimensional settings it is often appealing to have a prior that is concentrated at zero, favoring strong shrinkage of small signals and potentially a sparse estimator, while having heavy tails to avoid over-shrinkage of the larger signals. The Gaussian and double exponential priors are insufficiently flexible in having a single scale parameter and relatively light tails; in order to shrink many small signals strongly towards zero, the double exponential must be concentrated near zero and hence will over-shrink signals not close to zero.
